Title: What other services do you have other than CLO?
Content: We have other programs that you can utilize with CLO: CLO-SET and CLO-SET Connect. CLO-SET is an online cloud platform where you can share and communicate with your 3D Garments. CLO-SET CONNECT is an online marketplace where anyone who has a CONNECT account can buy and sell digital clothes. Through the CONNECT platform, you can find and download a various type of patterns, avatars (poses and motions), accessories, fabrics, and scenes for free or for charge. If you have any inquiries about CLOSET and CONNECT in terms of account, billing, or any technical issues, please refer to the CLO-SET Help Center or contact us. *CLO and CLO-SET are different service platforms and provide separate products, so you will need to purchase each product separately

Title: Parametric Pattern Creation(ver 7.0+)
Content: Objective Easily create Parametric Patterns by entering specs. Location Version 7.0 - 2024.0 Main Menu Editor Parametric Pattern Editor Version 2024.1+ Main Menu 2D Parametric Pattern Editor Operation Select the tool/menu indicated. Parametric Pattern Editor Window appears. Enter each value and click the Create button. The Parametric Pattern is created according to the entered specs, automatically arranged around the avatar and sewn. Title: Garment Fit Maps
Content: Objective Utilize four Garment Fit Maps in the 3D window to check 3D Gament's fit. Location 3D Window Hover the Mouse Over the 5th Icon Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: 3D Window Hover the Mouse Over the 5th Icon Four Garment Fit Maps appear. Refer to the table below and select the desired view icon. Icon Description Stress Map External stress causing garment distortion per area of the fabric appears in the range of color and numbers. Stress Map appears in total eight colors: Red indicates the strongest stress (100kPa) while blue indicates zero distortion (0.00kPa). Other numbers in between are expressed as gradation of two color. Strain Map Garment's distortion rate due to external stress appears in percentage. Stain Map appears in total eight colors: Red indicates 120% of distortion rate while blue indicates 100% (no distortion). Numbers in between are expressed as gradation of two color. Fit Map Fip Map shows tightness of the 3D Garment. Can't Wear appears in red indicating not wearable area. Very Tight appears in orange indicating very tight area. Tight appears in yellow indicating slightly tight area. Pressure Map Show or hide contact points between 3D Garment and Avatar. Based on the selected icon, Stress Map, Strain Map, Fit Map, or Pressure Map appear on the 3D Garment.

Title: What does each mode represent?
Content: Simulation Mode: Create and edit patterns in the 2D Window, working on garments, changing avatar poses, etc. in the 3D Window. Animation Mode: Record, play and edit garment animations. Print Layout Mode: Manually order patterns on prints to match texture placements in the 3D Window and calculate fabric consumption. Emulator Mode: Create physical properties for fabrics after measuring them out with the CLO Fabric Kit hardware. Modular Mode: Mix and match garment components such as sleeves and collars into blocks in order to evaluate and create new styles. Note: Found in the dropdown menu up to version 7.3 version 2024 and later features access to the Modular Library on the far left column of the software interface. UV Editor: Create UV maps of patterns, buttons, and zippers.

Title: Automatic Rigging & Converter
Content: Conver to Avatar Custom Rigging Objective Add joints or convert user data to CLO avatars and use CLO Avatar Editor. Location Main Menu Avatar Auto Convert to Avatar Operation Convert to Avatar Select the tool/menu indicated. Auto Convert to Avatar pop-up menu appears. The Auto Avatar Converter deletes all avatars in the 3D window. After setting the options below, click the Convert button. Menu Description Open the file to be converted Click the Open button on the right to load 3D dummy and scan files to be rigged and converted. Note: The Daz3D Genesis 8 version of the file is automatically recognized and converted into each high-quality avatar and accessory. The converted accessories are compatible with avatars of the same version and gender.(ver 7.3) Gender Set the gender of the avatar to be converted Converting Option Convert an avatar automatically or Maintain Custom Rig. Converted Output (AVT) CLO Skin Style The body shape of the original file is maintained and only the appearance is converted to a CLO avatar and joint points are added. Note: When converting to the avatar, size editing is not possible. The CLO Avatar Size Editor automatically fits into a realistic body shape based on thousands of actual scanned data so it cannot keep the body shape of the original file. Rigging only Only the joint points are added while maintaining both the body shape and appearance of the original file. Convert to size editable avatar Change the CLO avatar body shape so that the size can be edited while maintaining the appearance of the file to be converted and add joint points. Note: The conversion options below can be multi-selected and are compatible with the CLO avatar pose/motion provided in the Library after conversion. Save Click the Save button on the right and specify the path to save the converted avatar file. The file will be converted to an avatar with the options users set which may take 5-10 minutes. Custom Rigging Opacity Setting Change the opacity of the garment to make it easier to see the avatar. 3D Tool Bar Select the file to convert with Select/Move Tool. Property Editor Material (Selected) Basic Parameters Set the opacity to 50. Change the color of the file as required. Adjust Whole Body Main Menu Avatar Avatar Size Editor Align the CLO avatar with the Custom avatar by adjusting the below 3 points of measurement. Align the height of the shoulder and inseam. Choose one of the cases applicable. A.When using Total Height Click the up/down triangle button to the right of the Total Height number box to increase or decrease the avatar's height so the shoulder line is the same on both avatars. The shoulder shape of the Custom Avatar and the CLO avatar are different, so it is not necessary to perfectly match the shoulder position. Just using the triangle button to align with a similar shoulder line is sufficient, and you do not need to manually enter a precise value to align. Some errors are automatically adjusted during conversion. B. When using HPS Height and Inseam If the inseam height difference is too large when adjusting the shoulder line through Total Height, the shoulder line is adjusted according to the inseam measurement. After fixing, adjust the Inseam to fit. At this time, change the unnaturally deformed upper body naturally by adjusting the height of the CF/CB Neck to Waist. B-1) Set the Height type to the HPS Height. B-2) Align the shoulder height using the up/under triangle button in the input box. B-3) Details Inseam Height align the inseam height using the up/under triangle button. As the width of the adjustment of the inseam increases, the length of the upper body changes according to the Inseam. Since the CF/CB Neck to Waist value that controls the length of the upper body is fixed, the body shape may change unnaturally. In this case, it can be reflected in the result, so it is important to match the face and body shape of the avatars naturally. Recover naturally by following the method below. B-4) Details CF Neck to Waist/CB Neck to Waist. Press the triangle button on the right side of the number box in the opposite direction you pressed in the inseam to adjust the body shape until it looks natural. (e.g, if the length of the Inseam is shortened, the lengths of the two lower upper body lengths will be increased.) Normally, if you press the CF and CB triangle buttons the same number of times, the body shape is adjusted with a balanced front/back. Match the arm length Check the arm length once you adjust the shoulder height and the inseam. If the lengths to the wrist are different, click the up/down triangle button to the right of the CF Neck to Wrist number box to match the length to the avatar's wrist. Adjusting pose Avatar Display in the 3D window Show X-Ray Joints Match the pose and the joint points of the CLO avatar according to the pose of the Custom Avatar so that the two avatars overlap each other. Rotate the joints to make both avatars overlap. Note: If you can't see the overlapped avatars well when Show X-Ray Joints in on, click the joint and press Shift+X to keep using the Gizmo to adjust the joints with the textured avatar. To utilize the above method, you need to change the default gizmo of the 3D window to Local Coordinate, which is the same as the joint point view mode. Fitting the lower body Click the avatar's center joint point (purple) to bring up the gizmo and adjust the front/back position so the hips of the two avatars overlap. Click the hip joint to check both the front and the side, and align the ankles of the two avatars so that they overlap. Click the ankle point to adjust the insteps of the two avatars to overlap. Fitting the upper body Click the waist joint and rotate it from the side until the front of the avatar's neck and shoulders are overlapped. If you can't hit it all at once, align the shoulders first, then rotate the joint point on the side where the neck starts to align the front of the neck. Rotate the shoulder point to adjust the cuff to overlap. If it is not possible to align the wrist joint with the shoulder joint point, align the elbow joint first, then rotate the elbow joint to align the wrist joint. Click the wrist joint point to align the back of the hand. First, align the first finger joints/knuckle placements If the length of your finger is different, adjust the value of Avatar Size Editing Window Details Arm Hand to match the length. Click the joint point that is connected to the finger near the wrist joint point to align the gap between the fingers. Click the joint point where the finger starts to overlap the finger to the end. Rather than mesh the fingers of the two avatars, focus on locating the joint points at the appropriate places on the Custom avatar.

Follow the indicated path below: Main Menu 3D Garment Re-drape 3D Arrangement 3D Toolbar Re-drape 3D Arrangement Patterns are auto draped on the avatar based on its size.

Title: Adjust Avatar Size
Content: Objective Create an avatar with your own measurements. As CLO Avatar Editor is powered by thousands of real body scan data, even measurements not assigned by users automatically adjust to the most realistic body shape. Location Main Menu Avatar Avatar Editor Avatar Size Operation Load an Avatar (.avt). Select the tool/menu indicated. Measures appear on the Avatar. The editable measures appear in black, whereas the non-editable measures appear in grey. Refer to below graph and adjust the Avatar as needed. Option Description Avatar Size Easily select the size of the avatar in the Avatar Size Editor. Total Body Shape the overall body type with Avatar's height and chest width. In order to get realistic shapes for body parts without assignable measurements, use the Total Body option to create an overall shape and then insert measurements under the Details option. Height Assign Avatar's height. Because each person has a different head size, it is most accurate to create a full body shape based on HPS Height or Inseam. Total Height is the least accurate and is not recommended. Total Height Insert the height measured from the ground to the head. HPS Height Insert the height measured from the ground to the neck. Inseam Insert the height measured from the ground to the crotch. Proportion (ver 7.2 ) Adjust the ratio of the avatar's upper and lower body. Inseam Once the height between the floor and the legs is entered, the upper body automatically adjusts proportionally. CF Neck to Waist Once the height from the Front Neck Point to the waist is entered, the lower body automatically adjusts proportionally. Width Shape the overall body type based on Bust/ Under Bust Circumference, Weight. Weight (ver 7.1) Enter the weight to set its overall body width. After entering the weight, select the desired total body shape and it will be changed to the corresponding body shape. Details Configure Avatar's detailed measurements. A small error may be generated when entering measurements, and the error appears right next to each measurement. The actual applied measurements are displayed in the Avatar Measurement , so edit them more accurately by referring to them. Basic Adjust the value of the basic body measurements. Body measurements that cannot be adjusted are automatically changed to realistic body shapes based on actual data according to the adjusted measurements. Advanced Adjust the value of detailed body measurements. Advanced has more adjustable body measurments, but this may be more unnatural than the Basic option, as other measurements are not automatically adjusted and are fixed to the entered values. Simple (ver 7.1) When changing the width based on weight, simply adjust the size of the minimized body measurements. Show All Measurements Click the button at the top right of Details to check the all measurements. Open/ Save Open or save the avatar size measurements. Reset Reset the avatar's size to the default state.

Title: Topstitch Right-Click Pop-Up Menu
Content: Objective Edit topstitch using the right-click pop-up menu. Location Main Menu Materials Topstitch Edit Topstitch 2D Toolbar Edit Topstitch Operation Click the tool/menu indicated. Right click on the Topstitch to be edited. The right-click pop-up menu appears. Choose the desired option referring to the following table. Option Description Select All with Same Property Select the topstitches having the same properties as the selected topstitch. Assign to New Topstitch Assign the new topstitch to the selected topstitch. Delete Delete the topstitch Add Internal Line on Topstitch Create an Internal Shape right on top of the selected topstitch. Remove Linked Editing Remove the linked editing of the symmetric topstitches. Order (ver 7.0) Change the order of overlapping topstitches.

Title: Play Motion
Content: List of Contents Play Motion Pose Motion Play Motion - Play poses or motion files. - Main Menu Avatar Play Motion - 2D Toolbar Play Motion Pose - The Play Motion tool activates automatically when a pose file is loaded. - Click the Play Motion tool to pause the action. - Click again to replay the pose. Motion - The Play Motion tool can be selected when a motion file is loaded. - Click the Play Motion tool to play the motion. - Click the Play Motion tool to pause the action.

Title: Grading
Content: List of Contents Grading Create Size Group Add Size Delete Grading - Create and edit grading rules of a 3D Garment. - Create Size Group Object Browser Grading Tab +Add Add Size Object Browser Grading Tab Size Group (Select the One to be Edited) + Create Size Group - Click the + button in the Object Browsers Grading tab to add a new Size Group. - By default, a new Size Group is added and one Base Size is created. - Click the Size Group or the Size to view and edit its properties in the Property Editor. Add Size - Click the + button next to each Size under a Size Group. - A new Size is added and number is added at the end of the Size name in created order. - Toggle on the check box in front to each Size to assign as Base Size. Delete - Click the Delete icon on each Sizes right to delete the selected Size. - Similarly, click the Delete icon on each Size Groups right to delete the selected Size Group. - When a Size Group is deleted, its Sizes under the Group are also deleted. Note: In order to paste in a grading value, the selected point must have a Grading Size Group. Multiple grading values on multiple points cannot be pasted at once. However, one copied value can be pasted to multiple points. Use the shortcuts: Crtl+Z, Ctrl+Y to undo or redo copy and paste. Hide Patterns' grading rules using Show/Hide Grading.

Title: Edit Topstitch
Content: List of Contents Edit Topstitch Select Move Adjust Length Delete Edit Topstitch - Select, move, delete and adjust the selected Topstitchs length. - Navigate to the 2D toolbar and select the Edit Topstitch tool. - Or, navigate to the Main Menu &gt Material &gt Topstitch and select Edit Topstitch. Select When Only One Topstitch is on a Segment - Click the Topstitch to be selected. - The selected Topstitch is highlighted in pink. When Multiple Topstitches are on a Segment - When there are more than one Topstitches and on a segment, a pop-up menu appears showing all Topstitches on the selected segment. - Choose the desired Topstitch from the pop-up menu. Move - Click the Topstitch to be moved. - Drag to the desired location. Adjust Length - Click either end of a Topstitch to be edited. - Drag to freely adjust its length. Delete - Click the Topstitch to be deleted and hit the Delete key on the keyboard. - Or, right click on the Topstitch to be deleted and select the Delete option from the pop-up menu.

Title: Segment Darts
Content: List of Contents Add Dart Create Segment Darts Edit Segment Darts Add Dart - Create Darts on Pattern outlines. - Select the Edit Pattern tool from the 2D toolbar and right click on a point. Then, click Add Dart from the pop-up menu. Create Segment Darts - When the Dart window appears, adjust each option to create a Dart. Total Width - Set the total width of the Dart. Dart Arm Width - Set the half-length of the Dart. Length - Set the depth of the Dart. Edit Segment Darts - Select the Edit Pattern tool from the 2D toolbar. - Select all Pattern outlines that form the Dart. - The lines will be selected and highlighted in yellow. - Right-click on the selected lines and click the Edit Dart option from the pop-up menu. - Similar to when creating the Dart, adjust each option and click OK. - The Dart will be edited based on the settings.

Title: Edit Pattern
Content: List of Contents Edit Pattern Select Point/Line Select Multiple Points/Lines Move Point/Line Move Point/Line with Arrow Keys Move Point/Line with Specific Values Move Point/Line in Guidelines Move Point/Line in Slope Edit Pattern - Select and edit points and lines. - Select the Edit Pattern tool from the 2D toolbar. - Or, navigate to the Main Menu and select 2D pattern Edit Edit Pattern. Select Point/Line With Click - Navigate to the 2D window and click on the point or line to be selected. With Lasso Selection - With the Edit Pattern tool selected, double-click on the 2D window to activate the Lasso Selection. - Create marquee box around the points or lines to be selected. - Click the start point again to complete the marquee box. - All points and lines within the marquee box will be selected and highlighted in yellow. - The points and lines must be fully enclosed in the marquee box to properly select them. Select Multiple Points/Lines - While selecting the points and lines, hold down the Shift key on the keyboard to select multiple points and lines. - Or, click and drag to encompass all points and lines to be selected within the marquee box. Move Point/Line - With the Edit Pattern tool selected, click and drag the point or line to move the selected item. Move Point/Line with Arrow Keys - When the Edit Pattern tool selected, click the point or line to be moved. - Then, used the arrow keys on the keyboard to move the selected item. - When using the arrow keys, the selected item will move in 0.25 in increment. Move Point/Line with Specific Values - With the Edit Pattern tool selected, click and drag the point or line to be moved. - Right-click on the 2D window to open the Moving Distance window. - Enter Distance Moved and click OK. - The selected item will move based on the settings. Move Point/Line in Guidelines - With the Edit Pattern tool selected, click and drag the point or line to be moved. - While dragging the item, hold down the Shift key on the keyboard to activate the guidelines. - The selected point or line can be moved in a straight line or a diagonal line. Move Point/Line in Slope - With the Edit Pattern tool selected, click and drag the point or line to be moved. - While dragging the item, hold down the Ctrl key on the keyboard to activate the guidelines. - The selected point or line can be moved in the selected items slope.

Title: Delete
Content: Delete - Delete points, segments, Patterns and more. - Select the Transform Pattern tool from the 2D toolbar. Right-click on the objects to be deleted and select Delete from the pop-up menu. The selected object will be deleted. - Or, hit the Delete key on the keyboard after selecting the desired object to be deleted.

Title: Circumference Avatar Tape
Content: List of Contents Circumference Avatar Tape Create Avatar Tape Circumference Avatar Tape - Create Circumference Tape on Avatars. - Select the Circumference Avatar Tape tool from the 3D toolbar. - Or, navigate to Main Menu and select Avatar Avatar Tape Circumference Avatar Tape. Create Avatar Tape - To create a Circumference Tape on an Avatar, you must click three times. - Click on the Avatar to create the start point. - Move the cursor and click again to assign the direction of the Avatar Tape. - Make the third click to complete the Circumference Avatar Tape. - Hold down the Shift key on the keyboard to move the mouse in a straight line.

Location Main Menu Display Avatar Show Avatar Measurements 3D Window Avatar Display (Mouse-over) Show Avatar Measurements Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Display Avatar Show Avatar Measurements 3D Window Avatar Display (Mouse-over) Show Avatar Measurements All Avatar tape measures are now being displayed or hidden.

Location 2D Toolbar Transform Graphic Right-click Graphics Pop-up Menu Flip Horizontally / Flip Vertically Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: 2D Toolbar Transform Graphic Right-click Graphics Pop-up Menu Flip Horizontally / Flip Vertically The selected graphic image is now being flipped accordingly.

Title: [Popup] Show/Hide Button
Content: Objective Show or hide all buttons and buttonholes. Location 3D Garment Window 3D Garment Display (Mouse-over) Show Button Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: 3D Garment Window 3D Garment Display (Mouse-over) Show Button All buttons and buttonholes are now being hidden. Title: [Tool] Create Buttonhole
Content: List of Contents Create Buttonhole Input Measurement for Buttonhole Position Objective Create buttonholes and place them as desired. Location Main Menu Materials Button Buttonhole 3D Toolbar Buttonhole Operation Create Buttonhole Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Materials Button Buttonhole 3D Toolbar Buttonhole Click on a desired point on the 3D Garment or 2D Pattern. A buttonhole is created. Enter the number of garment layers and click OK. The buttonholes are now being created. Input Measurement for Buttonhole Position Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Materials Button Buttonhole 3D Toolbar Buttonhole Right-click on the 2D pattern where buttonholes would be placed. The Moving Distance window appears. Input desired measurements for accurate placement. Placement preview depending on the input value displays along the mouse in the 2D window. Click OK to place. Title: [Popup] Mirror Paste Button
Content: Objective Copy and mirror paste buttons (ver2.5.0). Location Main Menu Materials Button Select/Move Button Button Right-Click Pop-Up Menu Mirror Paste (Ctrl+R) 3D Toolbar Select/Move Button Button Right-Click Pop-Up Menu Mirror Paste (Ctrl+R) Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Materials Button Select/Move Button Button Right-Click Pop-Up Menu Mirror Paste (Ctrl+R) 3D Toolbar Select/Move Button Button Right-Click Pop-Up Menu Mirror Paste (Ctrl+R) Click Copy (Ctrl+C) from the pop-up menu. Right click on the copied button then click Mirror Paste (Ctrl+R) from the pop-up menu. Placement preview displays along the mouse in the 2D window. Click on a desired location to paste the buttons. Note: Before pasting buttons in place, right-click to access the Paste window where specific interval and number of buttons can be manually input for multiple copy and paste. When buttons are mirror-pasted, only locations are mirrored whereas other properties, such as Angle, are not.

Title: [2D Tool] Free Sewing
Content: Objective Freely establish Sewing Lines on Pattern outlines and Internal Shapes/Lines. Location Main Menu Sewing Free Sewing 2D Toolbar Free Sewing Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Sewing Free Sewing 2D Toolbar Free Sewing Click, drag and click on Pattern outline or Internal Shape/Line to establish the start and end points of the first half of the seam. Similarly, click again on another Pattern outline or Internal Shape/Line to establish the start point of the second half of the seam. Drag the mouse cursor as a blue point appears guiding the length of the first half of the seam. The mouse cursor snaps to the blue guide point. Be mindful to make the Directional Notches parallel to each other and click to complete the second half of the seam. Note: The face of the Directional Notch of a Sewing Line defers depending on the order of establishing the start and the end point of the Sewing Line. Right click while establishing the Free Sewing Line to enter the desired length of the Sewing Line in the Create Sewing Line window. Use the shortcut to establish M:N sewing lines. For more detail, please reference M:N Free Sewing.

Title: 3D Snapshot
Content: List of Contents Single View Multi View Objective Save 3D window snapshots from one or more angles as images. Location Main Menu File Snapshot 3D Window (F10) Operation Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. Enter desired file name and location, then click Save. Snapshot window appears. Set details as needed: Single View Image Size Preset Customize or select from provided preset options. Orientation Select from portrait or landscape orientation options. Width Set the width of the image. Height Set the height of the image. Unit Sets the unit of measurement for the image. Resolution Sets the pixels per inch for the image. From ver3.2.0, the image resolution (ppi) will automatically adjust depending on the selected paper size for optimal printing results. Option Transparent Background Save the image with a transparent background. Save All Colorways All colorways are saved. Save HTML File A HTML file of the snapshot is also saved. Reset Resets the options back to the program default settings. Multiview Preview Preset Mouse-over on the preview image Select desired view option from drop-down menu. Custom Customize view angle in the 3D window. Mouse-over on the preview image Click on the camera icon. Layout View Count Select the number of views to capture. Set it up to 10 views. (ver 5.2) Layout Select from horizontal/vertical/box layout options. Single Image Size Preset Customize or select from preset image size. Orientation Select from portrait or landscape orientation options. Width Set the width of the image. Height Set the height of the image. Unit Sets the unit of measurement for the image. Resolution Sets the pixels per inch for the image. From ver3.2.0, the image resolution (ppi) will automatically adjust depending on the selected paper size for optimal printing results. Option Transparent Background Save the image with a transparent background. Save Separate Images Save the multi-view in individual images. Save All Colorways All colorways are saved. Save HTML File (ver 5.2) A HTML file of the snapshot is also saved. Open / Save File Open Open all the setting options in *.mvs file format. Save Save all the setting options in *.mvs file format. Reset Resets the options back to the program default settings. Note: Garment Measurements can now be captured in 3D snapshots (ver4.1.0). In order to include Garment Measurements, toggle on the Show Garment Measurements icon in the 3D window. If you activate Show 3D Grid in the 3D window, you can utilize the grid guideline when you arrange a garment.

Title: 2D Pattern (MYU) Import
Content: Objective MYU is a file format that contains pattern information used by "Alpha Myu," one of the Pattern CAD software created by Yuka Alpha in Japan. Location Main Menu File Import MYU Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu File Import MYU The Open File window appears. Select the desired file to be imported and select OK. The Import DXF window appears. Adjust settings as needed. Note: The Import DXF options Scale Select Alpha Myu's default unit, "Millimeter." Option (Swap Cutting Line and Sewing Line) Check this option when Cutting Lines and Sewing Lines do not import properly. * Cutting Lines and Sewing Lines may be swapped depending on the adjusted settings when patterns were exported from other CAD programs.

Title: Reset 2D Arrangement
Content: Objective Spread and arrange the entire or selected Patterns in the 3D window identical to 2D window state. Location Selected Pattern 3D Toolbar Select/Move 3D Pattern Right-Click Pop-Up Menu Reset 2D Arrangement (Selected) All Pattern Main Menu 3D Garment Reset 2D Arrangement (All) 3D Toolbar Reset 2D Arrangement (All) Operation Selected Pattern Select a 3D Pattern to reset its arrangement identical to 2D window state. Note: Press Shift key on keyboard to select multiple Patterns. Follow the indicated guideline below: 3D Toolbar Select/Move 3D Pattern Right-Click Pop-Up Menu Reset 2D Arrangement (Selected) The selected Pattern is now being rearranged same as 2D window state. All Pattern Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu 3D Garment Reset 2D Arrangement (All) 3D Toolbar Reset 2D Arrangement (All) The entire Pattern is now being rearranged same as 2D window state.

Title: Add/Edit Bounding Volume
Content: Objective Add and edit Bounding Volume to add Arrangement Points to new objects. Location Main Menu Avatar Avatar Editor Arrangement Bounding Volume Add Operation Select the tool/menu indicated in Location A new Bounding Volumn named Pan is created at the bottom of the list of arrangement points and its properties appear at the bottom. Set the details of the Bounding Volume. Menu Description Board Check the list of currently added layouts and edit the properties of the layout by selecting the desired item. Name Rename the Bounding Volume. Joint Name 0 Set the position of the joint(X-ray joint point) where the Bounding Volume starts. Joint Name 1 Set the position of the joint(X-ray joint point) where the Bounding Volume ends. Shape (ver 6.0) Depending on the shape of the Avatar, the Bounding Volume is set to the Cylinder and Cuboid. Height Set the height of the Bounding Volume. Length X Adjusts the circumference of the left and right radii of the Bounding Volume. Length Y Adjusts the circumference of the top and bottom radii of the Bounding Volume. Round Corner (ver 6.0) It is active only when the Bounding Volume type is set to Cuboid. Adjust the radius of each corner. Hands/Feet If this option is activated, the length of the Bounding Volume is adjusted to the avatar's hands and feet. The moment you click that option, the entire Bounding Volume is refreshed. Note: If the order below/above the joint points is reversed, the left and right sides are flipped when arranging the Pattern.

Title: Convert to Hole/Internal Shape

Title: Mode
Content: Objective CLO provides total of seven Mode as follows: Simulation, Animation, Print Layout, Colorway, Comment, Emulator, and Modular Mode. Location Switch between Mode using the button on the right-top corner of the window. Operation Simulation Mode is a mode where it is possible to create and edit patterns in the 2D Window or animate draping of Garments, Poses, or Actions in the 3D Window. Animation Mode is a mode where it is possible to record, play and edit Garment animations. Print Layout Mode is a mode where it is possible to manually place patterns on prints to match texture placements in the 3D Window and to determine fabric yield. Colorway Mode is a mode where it is possible to test various color options on individual styles. Comment Mode is a mode where it is possible to communicate between users by adding comments such as explanations and revisions on the 3D Garments. Emulator Mode is a mode where it is possible to create custom physical properties for fabrics. Modular Mode is a mode where it is possible to mix and match Garment components, such as sleeves and collars, as blocks to test and create new styles.
